title: Apologia Quam Pro Se Misit Ad Anastasium Romanae Urbis Episcopum
author: Rufinus Aquileiensis
source: Translated by Claude from tmp389.tmp389.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: Alii asserunt, quod formatis in utero corpori- bus Deus quotidie faciat animas et infundat; alii quod g factas jam olim, idest, tunc cum omnia Deus creavit ex nihilo, nunc eas judicio suo dispenset in corpore. Hoc sentit et Origenes, et nonnulli ali Graecorum. Ego vero cum haec singula legerim, Dec teste, dico, quia usque ad praesens certi, et definiti aliquid de hac quaestione non teneo, sed Deo relia- quo scire, quid sit in vero, et si cui ipse revelare dignabitur.
passages.english: Others assert that, once bodies have been formed in the womb, God daily makes souls and pours them in; others that [souls] made long ago, that is, at the time when God created all things out of nothing, he now distributes into the body by his own judgement. This is the view of Origen too, and of some others among the Greeks. But I, though I have read each of these [views], say, with God as my witness, that up to the present I hold nothing certain and defined on this question, but leave it to God to know what is the truth, and to anyone to whom he himself will deign to reveal it.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'corpori- bus' read as corporibus, 'ali' as alii, 'Dec' as Deo, 'relia- quo' as relinquo; stray footnote mark 'g' omitted. The final clause ('et si cui ipse revelare dignabitur') is elliptical; it is taken as 'and [to leave it to be known by] anyone to whom he deigns to reveal it'.
